steps.text: Place water, olive oil, bread flour, salt, sugar, and yeast into a bread machine in the order listed, or follow the order recommended by the manufacturer if different. Run the Dough cycle, about 90 minutes.

Remove dough from the machine after the cycle is done. It will be quite sticky and wet; resist the temptation to add more flour. Place dough onto a generously floured board, cover with a large bowl or greased plastic wrap, and let rest for 15 minutes.

Lightly flour two baking sheets or line them with parchment paper. Cut dough with a serrated knife into two equal pieces; form each into piece into a 3x14-inch oval. Tranfer loaves to the prepared baking sheets and dust lightly with flour. Cover and let rise in a draft-free place for approximately 45 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Spritz loaves with water, then place onto the middle rack of the preheated oven. Bake until golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ciabatta Bread
raw_recipe.description: Ciabatta bread is an Italian classic. With this recipe, you make the dough in a bread machine and then bake the loaves in the oven until golden brown.

review.reviewBody:
Good results!

As a culinary student I've tried and failed with bread many times before getting some decent results. Here's what I've found that may help: 
1) Proof your yeast as directed (mixing water, yeast, & sugar)-- if it doesn't start bubbling or frothing after 10 min, throw it out. Either the yeast is dead (check expiration date) Or you killed it with HOT tap water > 120 degrees F kills yeast. Optimal temp is LUKE warm around 100F. 
2) Mist the bread with water every 3 min for the first 10 min. Why? This does 3 things. Prevents the crust from forming too fast thus restricting the rising process. It moisens the crust just enough so it doesn't brown/burn at the end of the baking period - you get a golden brown instead of a dark heavy crust. And it finally makes the crust crispier. This is a very important step. It also helps if you have a bowl of water in the oven to increase the humidity percentage. Professional ovens have adjustable humidity controls which add moisture in. Why only 10 min? You can mist for longer but you'll end up with a thin white crust instead of golden brown. Once the bread has risen to its full potential (within the 1st 10 min or so depending on the size of the loaf), then you want it to start becoming golden brown.

Baking is regarded as being harder than cooking because of the exactness in ratios of the ingredients. 
Hope some of my hard lessons learned helps you -- Best of luck!

I made this with old instant yeast and old active dry yeast around double the recipe amount total, and a mixture of 1/3 cu. bread flour, 1 cu. whole wheat flour, and the remainder white AP flour, with an additional 1/4 cu. because it usually seems necessary for me. I mixed the yeast and flour together by hand before mixing in the salt and then the liquids and so on. My stand-up mixer performed the mixing of the water and kneading. I had to stop and mush the dough ball a little bit after adding the oil, because sometimes it slipped off the hook, rather than be kneaded. Maybe my bowl is too big.
Regardless, the bread turned out tasty and spongy. I sprayed it a bunch of times with water and baked it in the oven with a bowl of water (maybe the bowl was too small) to try to get a crispier crust, but it didn't quite turn out that way. It still works well for its intended purpose, dipping in olive oil, basalmic vinegar, garlic and spices. Very tasty. The bread smells good.
I have to admit after it rose, I was a little concerned that it wouldn't turn out well because it didn't spring back after I pushed it in, but that's probably because my yeast was half-dead. It seems to be the same thickness as the bread pictured on the recipe page.
Anyway, enjoy!

I don’t have a bread machine so I mix it by hand. I use 3 teaspoons of active dry yeast which I let proof with the 1 1/2 cups of warm water (around 110 degrees) and sugar for about 10 minutes then I added in the flour, salt and oil. I kneaded the dough for about 10 minutes adding a little flour to form a smooth ball and to get the excess dough off my hand.

I made this using 120grams of King Arthur Bread flour per cup...so total of 390 grams on a dough cycle in a breadmaker. The dough was comparable to a thick yogurt or muffin batter. I literally poured it into a tall, round cake pan and let it rise there; kneading it would be impossible. When it rose, I baked it...and it was delicious. I'm guessing people are using actual cup measures which often ends up being 1-2 tablespoons or more per cup. Has anyone figured out the correct grams of flour for this recipe? Thanks.

I make it once a week. super versatile. variations I have been successful with: 1. 1 tbs minced fresh rosemary plus 1/4 cup minced oil cured olives mixed in 2. replace 1 cup of flour with 1 cup of rye flour plus add 1/4 cup of caraway seeds

Mine turned out wonderful! Yes, I made a change for the best and the easiest way... still used the same ingredients but in the following order: Water/ Olive Oil/Flour/Sugar/Salt/ Added 1 tsp dry rosemary leaves/Salt/ Machine yeast... Then... Turned on my bread maker: Menu: French Bread/2 pd size/Dark crust! That's all!! The best tasting crusty bread ever! Try it!!!!

These bread machine recipes make baking simplified . I use the recipe ingredients however, I had to make some adjustments. I have a convection oven so I bake the bread at 400°, I didn’t have the bread flour but I did have OO pasta flour, so I added vital gluten - 2 tablespoons as Alexa told me that OO pizza flour didn’t have as much protein as bread flour. I was very surprised how soft the dough was an after a 15 minute rest after taking it out of the bread machine. I think I’ll use this technique with all the breads I make! I baked it about 20 minutes at 400°. It made two decent size loaves. It tasted wonderfully soft and had a nice chew! Thank you for making me successful.

Really good bread. Yes, the dough is VERY sticky and somewhat hard to work with , but the end result is SO good. I have also used coarse salt on the bread while baking and have tried adding dry Italian herbs, both really good. Finally, I didn't spritz while baking, but filled a 13x9 half full with water and put it on the rack below the bread before turning the oven on. This worked great as well.

I made this pretty much as stated. After the bread machine said the dough was done rising, I let it continue to rise another few minutes, like 15 or so. I put parchment on my stoneware and sprinkled with cornmeal. I removed the dough with floured hands, VERY sticky, shaped into loaves as best I could, right on my parchment. I heated my oven to 200 degrees for 1 minute, turned it off, covered the loaves with a damp towel and let them rise 40 minutes. Removed them, preheated to 430 F, baked 30 minutes. Fabulous.

I make this bread in my bread machine. I make it as white bread, or I make it as whole wheat (2 cups bread flour, 1 cup whole wheat flour, 1/4 cup of ground Flax seed. I am a type 2 diabetic so using less sugar and more fiber is important to me. This bread is delicious!

I have made this before two times. Sooooo good. I don’t remember if I doubled the dough cycle. My bread machine has a dough cycle that is 45 minutes. This says do dough cycle for 90 minutes. Should I just do the dough cycle two times or assume my bread machine does it enough in 45 minutes

I used my stand mixer. Right off the bat, it was pancake batter thin. So when I poured it on the well floured surface, pouring is no exaggeration. I covered and let it rest. Then when there was no intervention from a bakery fairy, I kneaded much of that generously flouring on my board into the bread. Still it was too wet to cut with a serrated knife but I managed to get 2 equal “loaf “. Used my French bread pans to provide structure at the last minute. Halfway thru the rise in the photo and I’m holding my breath it doesn’t slide off the end. I don’t think this is a recipe for me. Something is not right
Very easy to follow and I made the entire loaf in my bread maker. Great tasting bread!! I used artisan bread flour with the quick rise yeast and it came out Chef 💋!!!
It came out perfect!

Soooo easy to make using the “dough” setting on my bread maker. I made it 3 times in my first week. But instead of 2 long loaves, I make it into one round loaf — and add sliced green olives. After the first 15 minute rest under a large bowl, I add the olives and put the dough onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Cover with the bowl and let rise for 45 minutes. Remove the bowl and pop into the oven for 30 minutes — this bread is soooo good. Family loves it.

I make this about every 3 days. It replaces buying Italian bread at the store. I make it for potlucks at church. It's a hit. The key is to follow the directions to use with your bread machine. And Bread Flour is a MUST. In fact I just bagged 2 loaves 15 min ago. :)
Soo wet, basically had to pour it onto baking trays and fold over like an omelette. However, it turn out delicious.

Mixed up exactly as the instructions said. Dough came out really sticky and had a bit of difficulty cutting in half, but succeeded! Popped in the oven (convection) for about half an hour and amazing fresh bread! Definitely will do again!
Perfect! Followed exactly as written. Delicious! Thank you for sharing your recipe.
